cards.text: David is king, and he's got construction going up all over the City of David. Buildings for himself, sure. But he also prepares a place for the ark of God.

cards.question: In the City of David, David builds a stone temple for the ark of God.

cards.text: No temple. David pitches a tent for the ark. Then, before anybody lifts a finger, he lays down a rule about who gets to carry it.

cards.question: David's rule for the ark of God: no one may carry it but who?
David says the Levites carry the ark because the LORD has ___ them to carry it and minister before Him forever.

cards.text: Then David assembles ALL Israel in Jerusalem to bring the ark up to the place he prepared. That's not a group text, friend, that's a whole nation on reply-all.
Then he gathers the descendants of Aaron and the Levites, six clans in all. Each clan brings its chief and somewhere between 80 and 220 relatives, starting with Uriel and 120 Kohathites.
David calls in the priests Zadok and Abiathar, plus the six Levite chiefs. Now it's the kind of meeting where NOBODY is checking their phone.

cards.question: David tells the heads of the Levite families that before they bring up the ark, they and their relatives must do something. What is it?

cards.text: Then David gets honest about the first time they tried to bring up the ark. He says the LORD their God burst forth in anger against them.

cards.question: David tells the Levite heads why the LORD burst forth in anger the first time. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They moved the ark at night

cards.question: David admits that the first time, they didn't consult the LORD about the proper order.

cards.text: So the priests and Levites consecrate themselves to bring up the ark. Getting ready FIRST. Me? I read my oven manual AFTER the smoke alarm.

cards.question: Time to move the ark of God. How do the Levites carry it this time?

answers.text: On a cart pulled by oxen
On a wagon pulled by mules

cards.question: The Levites carry the ark this way because ___ had commanded it, in line with the word of the LORD.

cards.text: David also has another job for the leaders of the Levites: appoint some of their relatives for something special.

cards.question: David wants the Levite leaders to appoint some of their relatives for the ark's big day. What job does he have for them?
David wants the singers to lift up their voices with ___.

cards.text: Then comes a long list of names: Heman, Asaph and Ethan on bronze cymbals, others on harps and lyres, priests on trumpets, and guardians for the ark. Chenaniah the head Levite directs the music because he was highly skilled, so he's the guy who hears one wrong note from across the room.
Then David, the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands head out with rejoicing to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

cards.question: David, the elders and the commanders go to bring up the ark of the covenant. Whose house do they bring it from?

cards.text: And this time, God helps the Levites carrying the ark. You know how a couch gets SO much lighter the second a friend grabs the other end? Yeah.

cards.question: Because God helped the Levites carrying the ark, what do they do?

answers.text: Sacrifice seven bulls and seven rams
Sacrifice twelve lambs and a goat
Rest seven days beside the road

cards.text: Now, the outfits. The Levites carrying the ark, the singers and Chenaniah the music director are all in robes of fine linen.

cards.question: King David skips the linen and wears his own royal robe instead.

cards.text: David's in a robe of fine linen too, same as the crew, and he also wears a linen ephod. The king matches his team, and I LOVE it.

cards.question: So all Israel brings up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with ___.

cards.text: Rams' horns, trumpets, cymbals, harps and lyres: friend, this is NOT a quiet Tuesday. Then, as the ark enters the City of David, Saul's daughter Michal looks down from a window.

cards.question: Michal, Saul's daughter, looks down from a window as the ark enters the City of David. What does she see?

answers.text: King David weeping beside the ark
King David arguing with the priests

cards.question: Michal is glad to see King David dancing and celebrating.

cards.text: A whole city celebrating, and one heart up in that window that isn't. Hold that thought, friend. The ark's in town, but this story still has pages left.

findings.problem: "He's got construction going up all over the City of David" stretches the text. 1 Chronicles 15:1 says only that David constructed buildings for himself in the City of David. "All over" is stated as fact, not as a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The joke contrasts the Levites "Getting ready FIRST" with Papa Dorin reading his oven manual "AFTER the smoke alarm." Cards 10 to 12 just told the baker about the first attempt, when the LORD burst forth in anger (1 Chr 15:13). So Israel is also preparing after the disaster, the same as Papa Dorin. The contrast doesn't hold, and the baker is left asking "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The passage's last detail, that Michal despised David in her heart (1 Chr 15:29), is never stated. Card 15 only establishes that she isn't glad, and card 16 softens it to "one heart up in that window that isn't" celebrating. The baker leaves without the key fact. "A whole city celebrating" also stretches the text: verse 28 says all Israel brought up the ark, not that the city celebrated.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
